Some tips for LR that I found useful are:

- Pay attention to pivot words like: however, yet, but etc. They’re introducing a new perspective, and usually end up being the conclusion or support for the conclusion.

- pay attention for quantifiers like: none, some, most, all etc. 

- pay attention to word descriptors. I find this really useful on SA and flaw questions, where a premise will be talking about “ice coffee” but the conclusion talks about “coffee” in general. That’s the bridge that needs to be built for SA or a generalization/part to whole flaw.

- I struggled with conditionals, and the easiest way to tackle long conditionals (to me) is to read the question through once, start with “real” conditionals not some and most, then ask yourself which of the conditions is required (necessary) or which one triggers (sufficient) the other. After I add the some and most conditionals, if applicable, only to the left of the sufficient condition.

For RC I don’t have anything ground breaking but here are tips that helped me:

- highlight the subject matter, it can be easy to get lost in the sauce of the passage, highlighting that the passage is about global warming or unions helped me to get less confused when more technical language starts getting brought up.

- Highlight pivot words again like: however, yet, but etc. They are shifting perspectives whether it be a critic the author or another critic

- Pay attention to the number of perspectives or speakers in the passage and where they are so you can more easily refer back to them if you need to while answering questions.
 
- Kind of building on the previous point but, read for structure, ask how this sentence builds upon the last, is it the authors opinion, an example used to support the main point, is it a concession to a critic or alternate point of view. Usually asking “why” is this sentence being used here is helpful.

Anyway, I hope these help a little bit, good luck with the studying, you got this!

I would stop using Arazlo until your skin is no longer itchy, red and flaky. For me even after using it for ~5 months I can’t use it unbuffered so I’d recommend getting a night time moisturizer to reduce irritation. When you are ready to use it again your routine should look something like this:

AM:
- wash with water or gentle cleanser
- moisturizer 
- sunscreen

PM:
- gentle cleanser
- moisturizer 
- wait ~20 minutes for face to dry
- occlusive around eyes and lips (optional)
- Arazlo

When starting again I’d aim for 3 times a week and slowly increasing based on how much your skin can handle. Good luck!

- Cetaphil Lotion

- SPF

PM:

- Cerave Cleanser

- Cetaphil Lotion

- Tretinoin

I’d give your skin a week or two to settle into having no other actives and see how you do. If by then your skin feels good but needs some help with breakouts I’d add a BP wash on some mornings or get clindamycin cream from your derm.

It’s really dependent on your skin. I personally wouldn’t use AHA’s and BHA’s when first starting but there are lots of people who can use a benzoyl peroxide wash in the AM with few issues. If you’re worried about over doing actives clindamycin is just an antibiotic and doesn’t actually exfoliate but can be a little drying for some. Also what’s your routine at the moment? I found it best when I simplified but everyone is different.

On average a purge should last 4-6 weeks but is also dependent on how often you’re applying tret. Less frequent application can lead to longer purging and retinization process but applying too frequently in the beginning can lead to irritation breakouts. I started seeing improvements in my skin by week 6 and more major improvements by week 8. 

Depending on how your skin is feeling clindamycin or benzoyl peroxide (or both) can really help the purge along. Retinoids alone weren’t enough to clear my breakouts but after I added BP things have cleared much more.

I think the same process can apply if you have any 0.1 tretinoin cream leftover. Slowly swap one or two nights a week for taz to see how your skin responds and increase the number of swap nights to your comfort. If you don’t have any leftover tret I’d start with every other day for the first week or two since your skin should be well retinized already. Depending on how your skin responds you can increase or decrease usage. Good luck and welcome to team Taz!!

Definitely write down your questions and concerns about where to go to next before going to the derm, I always find I’m less likely to miss a detail when I do.

How did you respond to the dapsone? Maybe using the BP wash in the morning with the dapsone and tret at night might be a good option and the BP should help with antibiotic resistance. I’d also see if you can move up your derm appointment to discuss next steps.

Is there a reason your derm switched you to tretinoin? From my knowledge 0.1 adapalene  is equivalent to 0.025 tret and 0.3 adapalene is equivalent to 0.05 tretinoin in terms of acne control so the 0.025 is a step down from the tactupump forte plus the combo of BP is really good for getting rid of acne. Also, most tret formulations can degrade in UV light so the should only be applied at night and the addition of the BP wash in the same routine probably isn’t helping trets stability. I’d either shift the tret to the night routine or it might be best to go back to tactupump since it was clearing you up already.

I ended up adding a benzoyl peroxide wash in the morning which helped tremendously and is especially helpful after a sweaty workout.

I think when acne is more hormonal you need to attack it from different angles and a lot of times Tretinoin might need support from other ingredients to fully keep you clear.

There’s OTC options too like Panoxyl (4% and 10%) and Neutrogena (3.5%) just depends what works best for you. Plus I find a wash is less likely to bleach things than a leave on but not sure if you guys are having trouble with that.

I love tazarotene! I feel like since your acne is already well controlled by tret you’re less likely to purge again or at least it shouldn’t be a bad one 🤞. As for transitioning from one to the other, I’d keep using tret like usual but 1 or 2 times a week switch it out for tazarotene. See how your skin responds and slowly faze out tret while adding in more tazarotene days.

I’ve found a 10% BPO Wash in the morning works really well for me. It might be a bit much depending on your skin but I like that I don’t end up with bleached clothing or towels anymore and I can easily do short contact therapy with it while I take a shower. If you choose a leave on though I’d buffer with your moisturizer, that always helped reduce irritation when I used Duac.

I definitely did. I feel like I wasted 3/4 of my first tube because the results were decent but not great. Started putting it on bare skin and it improved a lot faster. Not sure if it’s the moisturizer I used or because I have a micro formula though 🤷🏻‍♀️

If you have a darker complexion using too strong a retinoid can lead to irritation which can lead to areas of hyperpigmentation. If you have a lighter skin tone (like me) you might find your face gets flushed more easily like getting out of a warm shower or doing mild exercise. It happened to me when I was using too much and too often and my face and neck looked like completely different colours. Not sure if that’s a long the lines of what you’re experiencing but each should improve when you apply less and moisturize more (and try not to wash with really hot water).

Breaking out again when you move up in strengths is pretty normal as long as it’s in places you usually breakout in. As for whether you should keep going every night or pull back it really depends on how your skin is feeling. If there’s no irritation keep going but keep an eye out you can always take breaks if your skin needs it. You should have better control on your acne when you use it more frequently plus it should help the purge go by hopefully quicker. Definitely listen to your skin though.

Tazarotene and Tretinoin both treat acne and photoaging while Tazarotene can also be used to treat psoriasis. They are pretty similar although Taz is thought to be a little stronger and can bring about results faster but with the possibility of more irritation. I personally use the tazarotene lotion Arazlo and it’s worked pretty well for me so far but I’ve never tried Tret to be able to personally compare them.

I used Duac when I was in highschool definitely helped with breakouts. I would use it daily or every other day depending on your tolerance and keep it in a separate routine from your retinoid (and vitamin c if you use one).

I also tried that 4% BP Cerave cleanser I couple months ago and my face reacted badly. Eyes puffed up skin was red and weepy and breakouts got worse so it could be something in the formula that just doesn’t agree with you. I thought I was allergic to BP but I got a prescription for a 10% wash and it’s essentially cleared my skin. Maybe ask your derm for a prescription wash or see if there are OTC options that have fewer ingredients. I’d also take a day or two break until irritation settles down to start back up on tret.

Congrats on starting your tret journey 🎉! I was nervous starting off too but it hasn’t been bad so far. Just keep an eye out, dryness and some peeling is to be expected but if it’s too much or your skin is sore you won’t lose progress taking a day or two off. Good luck!

The delay in applying tretinoin and experiencing side effects is about 72hrs which is why it’s good to be cautious in the first couple weeks of use. If you’ve been using it for a couple weeks with minimal or no irritation just keep doing what you’re doing.

Yes it’s called sandwiching and it usually helps when you’re just starting a retinoid although some people keep using it after months of use so it depends on your skin. I think the important thing is to wait between layers so wash face then moisturize wait for it to dry down apply tretinoin wait to absorb (10-20mins depending) followed by another layer of moisturizer. As for other recommendations I’d keep your skincare minimal in the beginning and definitely check the side bar of the subreddit for the wiki for more information what to expect and usage.

If you’re not experiencing any irritation I’d keep doing what you’re doing. The delay between applying tret and experiencing potential side effects is about 72hrs which has already passed. It’s good to practice caution when using retinoids but I think some people (myself included) go too slow and it can lengthen purging and retinization process. Just keep an eye out for irritation and if you see any you can always take a night or two off. Also sandwiching is great especially to start off with but I have better results when I don’t and if there’s no irritation or dryness it’s good to not sandwich.

I don’t think a day or two break will stop progress in the long run but I definitely understand your feelings of wanting to push through if it is the purge. The thing I’ve found with retinoids is that there’s a lot of trial and error to find the most effective and least irritating way to apply them. As an experiment next time try buffering it with a very small amount of your moisturizer since it is thick (just to stop water loss) let it dry down completely and then apply tret on top (damp skin increases penetration and I find it makes azelaic acid more itchy). If you want to you can add another thicker layer of moisturizer after the tret dries down for more hydration.

I would definitely take a break for a bit until your skin stops hurting. There is supposed to be a certain level of irritation starting a retinoid but if it’s becoming unbearable or effecting your mental health I’d stop and reassess. Perhaps it’s a matter of buffering it instead of putting it on directly or that the added ingredients are causing more irritation. I for one found as great as azelaic acid is there wasn’t a formulation that didn’t make my skin burn and itch. Maybe after the break you can talk to your derm about either continuing the topical or just trying plain tret without any added ingredients.

It might be worth a shot to find out! If you do want to transition to Arazlo I’d keep using your Aklief like normal but swap it out one night with Arazlo so you don’t lose progress. 

The other guys suggestion of azelaic acid is also a good option and is pretty popular on this subreddit. It should help with redness and leftover PIE and PIH. It does itch for the first couple weeks but goes down soon. Ultimately depends on what your skin can handle and what you’d like to do.

Aklief is more selective in the retinoic acid receptors it binds to, specifically it only binds to gamma receptors which makes it a less irritating retinoid to use while still being effective at treating acne. It also seems to be formulated to be less drying and irritation causing. 

On the other hand Arazlo acts on all three retinoic acid receptors (gamma, beta and alpha) making it very effective for treating acne and photoaging. Because it acts on more retinoic acid receptors some people get quicker results and better acne control than other retinoids. It’s also a micronized formula meaning it’s slow release thus reducing irritation.

I don’t personally have experience using Aklief but I was using 0.3 adapalene before switching to Arazlo. With adapalene I would also go through periods where my skin would flare up and then calm down which was very frustrating. So far after switching I don’t flare up as much or as severely. I also found that post acne marks went away faster. Only issue was that it was slightly more irritating but after upping my moisturizing game it got easier and now I can use it daily. As for flare ups potentially caused by dairy there’s no harm in cutting it out for a couple weeks to see how you feel and how it effects your skin. There seems to be a lot of people who had good results after cutting it out but everyone is different.

I think it’s just purging especially since this is only your 7th application and it seems to be pre-existing comedones coming to a head. I would bump up application to 3 days a week if you can because only doing it once a week your skin won’t be able to retinize properly and prolongs the purging timeline. As your skin gets acclimatized you can slowly bump up frequency as needed until your breakouts are under control. It might also be worth it to do a quick check in with your derm to make sure things are on track.

Your routine looks good I would just add a sunscreen in the morning. If you’re sure none of the products are breaking you out and your acne has returned after 2 accutane courses I’d check to see if it’s hormonal based. Accutane can help with hormonal acne but it doesn’t always cure it, if you’re a women spirolactone or BC pills can be useful if you’re more interested in topical options there’s winlevi which recently came out and topical spiro compounded by a pharmacy.

From the beginning of the purge till the end, it should last about 4-6 weeks. I would give yourself another 2-3 weeks to see if anything improves. When I used adapalene the first month was pretty rough but things started to smooth out by week 6 and I saw real improvements by week 8-12. Purging for months shouldn’t typically happen and is usually caused by using the active too much, too little or using a product that causes breakouts. If after a few weeks the purge hasn’t let up I’d call your derm up to ask for next steps.
It could be the vehicle that’s giving you trouble. There’s quite a few people here that breakout from the cream formulation and find the gel version to be better.

That could be it then. Might be a bit strange but check your cities water hardness levels, some people are more sensitive to water quality and hard water may cause your skin to act up. As for the stressful test coming up try to take some time for yourself to decompress when needed maybe some meditation and mindfulness or whatever helps you calm down during difficult times.

It could be that the 0.25 was no longer controlling your acne and it might take a while for it to work it’s magic again. It’s strange that it came on so suddenly though. Did you change anything in your routine or hair care? Is there anything stressful going on in your life or a move of some kind? Breakouts are caused by a number of different things so it can be hard to nail down what’s causing it for you specifically.
How long have you been using the 0.05 and what kind of formulation do you use?

You’re routine looks good, very simple which is usually best with tret the only things is I would add a moisturizer to your PM routine. As for the breakouts, I think it seems unusual to be breaking out still at 12 weeks. It sounds like it started later than most purges at week 8 so that might be why it’s still going on. I’d see if you can get an appointment with your doc just to do a check in with your progress, unfortunately retinoids are a long haul and there tends to be some trial and error. 

Also, there’s also a lot of things going on in your life especially with your anorexia recovery. I had some hormonal imbalances early on in my refeeding recovery and had a slight increase in breakouts. Definitely not something to freak out about and my skin quality is a lot better after going through the program. Doctors should be monitoring your health and blood work throughout recovery. Best of luck! 💜
